statement.p: Find the length of the curve x = 4t-1,\quad y = t-3, z = 3+3t, for 1 \le t \le 3.

p.em: (Think of second way that you could calculate this length, too, and see that you get the same result.)

static.solution: \hbox{Length} = \int_1^3 \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2 + (z'(t))^2}\,dt = \int_{1}^{3} \sqrt{(4)^2+(1)^2+(3)^2}\,dt = 2\sqrt{26}. This is the length of a straight line from the point (3,-2,6) to (11,0,12).
